Moment of a Force and the Principle of Moments (Seesaw)

Sum of anticlockwise moments
—
Sum of clockwise moments
—
Net moment (clockwise +)
—
Balanced?
—
Drag the children along the seesaw, or type their distances. Distances are measured from the pivot: negative = left of the pivot.
  • Moment = force × perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of action of the force.
  • Here each force is a child's weight, W = mg, with g = 10 m s-2.
  • A weight on the right of the pivot turns the seesaw clockwise. A weight on the left turns it anticlockwise.
  • By the principle of moments, the seesaw balances only when the sum of clockwise moments equals the sum of anticlockwise moments.
  • The seesaw starts locked at the horizontal level, so each perpendicular distance is simply the distance along the plank, and the moments are worked out for that position.
  • When we remove the lock, if the moments are not equal, it turns until one end hits the ground. (Once it tilts, the perpendicular distances get shorter, so the moments are no longer shown; moving a child locks it level again.)
  • The seesaw is a light plank pivoted at its centre, so its own weight has no moment.
